page: Amazon Web Services c9g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, operating under the Nitro hypervisor. The CPU architecture is arm64, with a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.4xlarge demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, achieving top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench text processing. The Passmark memory score also ranks in the top tier. Multi-threaded performance is strong, as evidenced by bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores. For specialized workloads, the instance delivers strong performance in static web serving throughput and database operations, alongside average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations. Large-model LLM inference data is unavailable, but small-model text generation reaches top-tier speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture and dedicated physical core allocation provide high compute density without hyperthreading overhead. This makes the instance highly efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The c9g.4xlarge is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, single-threaded data compression tasks, text processing, database operations, and lightweight LLM inference.
